description: A two-panel composite figure combining grain-size distribution statistics with a grain-refinement curve fit for Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel processed by multiaxial forging (MAF). (a) plots area fraction (y-axis, 0.0-0.5) against grain size (x-axis, logarithmic, labelled 0.1, 1 and 10 µm) with four curves given in the legend as MAF-0 (black), MAF-1 (red), MAF-3 (blue) and MAF-5 (green); each curve is also identified by a boxed text label with a leader arrow. All four distributions are near zero below roughly 5 µm and rise steeply at coarser sizes; MAF-0 is the broadest and reaches the highest area fraction (just above 0.3, near 30-40 µm), whereas MAF-5 is the narrowest and lowest (peaking near 0.09 around 10-20 µm), so the distribution shifts to finer sizes and becomes more uniform with increasing pass number. (b) plots grain size (y-axis, 10-55 µm) against equivalent plastic strain (x-axis, 0.0-2.5): black squares are the "Measured" values and the red dashed "Predicted using Eq. (8)" curve is an exponential fit. An inset table gives d = 50*exp(-k3*x), k3 = 0.63999 ± 0.03785, R-Square (COD) = 0.99052.

observations.observation: Panel (a) legend and boxed annotations name exactly four sample conditions: MAF-0 (black), MAF-1 (red), MAF-3 (blue) and MAF-5 (green).
Panel (a) axes are 'Area fraction' (linear, ticks 0.0-0.5 in steps of 0.1) versus 'Grain size (µm)' on a logarithmic axis with printed tick labels 0.1, 1 and 10 only.

In panel (a) the MAF-0 (black) curve reaches the largest area fraction shown, slightly above the 0.3 gridline, at grain sizes near the right-hand limit of the plot, while the MAF-5 (green) curve stays lowest, peaking just below the 0.1 gridline near 10 µm.

In panel (a) the distributions are extremely asymmetric: all four curves lie near zero area fraction below about 5 µm and then rise steeply, with the MAF-1 (red) and MAF-3 (blue) curves showing sharp narrow spikes at coarse grain sizes.
Panel (b) shows four 'Measured' black square data points, read off the axes as 50 µm at strain 0.0, 35 µm at ~0.5, 20 µm at ~1.4 and 13 µm at ~2.3.
The inset table in panel (b) prints the fit equation d = 50*exp(-k3*x) together with k3 = 0.63999 ± 0.03785 and R-Square (COD) = 0.99052.
Panel (b) axes are 'Grain size (µm)' (10-55, linear) versus 'Equivalent plastic strain' (0.0-2.5, linear).
The caption states that (a) plots area fraction against grain size and (b) shows the effect of equivalent plastic strain on grain size.
The citing text states that the solutionized and quenched material has grains of average size 50 µm, and that this value is also verified from optical microstructure measurement.

The citing text states that, during MAF, the initial austenite grain size is reduced to 35 µm and 20 µm after the first and third pass respectively, and to approximately 13 µm after five passes at a total strain of 2.3.

The citing text reports that Eq. (8) was fitted to the Fig. 8(b) plot of imposed equivalent strain versus grain size and that k3 was found to be 0.639, matching the value printed in the panel (b) inset table (0.63999).

The citing text attributes grain refinement to grain subdivision and more intricate grain boundaries caused by the plastic deformation during forging, producing lamellar grains with transverse dimension of about 13 µm.
The citing text states that the grain sizes shown in this figure were measured from EBSD analysis.

subfigures.description: Line plot of area fraction (0.0-0.5, linear) versus grain size (µm) on a logarithmic x-axis labelled 0.1, 1 and 10. Four curves are shown, listed in the legend as MAF-0 (black), MAF-1 (red), MAF-3 (blue) and MAF-5 (green), and each is additionally marked by a boxed annotation with an arrow (MAF-0, MAF-1, MAF-3, MAF-5). All curves are near zero at fine sizes and rise at coarse sizes; MAF-0 has the highest and broadest tail, MAF-5 the lowest and narrowest.

Scatter plot with fitted curve of grain size (µm, 10-55) versus equivalent plastic strain (0.0-2.5). Four black square markers labelled 'Measured' sit at strains 0.0, ~0.5, ~1.4 and ~2.3 with grain sizes 50, 35, 20 and 13 µm; a red dashed line labelled 'Predicted using Eq. (8)' is an exponential decay through them. An inset table states d = 50*exp(-k3*x), k3 = 0.63999 ± 0.03785, R-Square (COD) = 0.99052.

unreadable_items: panel (a): no tick label is printed on the logarithmic x-axis beyond 10 µm, so the exact upper grain-size limit of the axis is not explicitly stated
panel (a): the numeric values of the sharp coarse-size spikes of the MAF-1 (red) and MAF-3 (blue) curves are not annotated and cannot be read exactly from the axes
